Getting around

On foot or by mountain bike (MTB). Motorcycles and mopeds of any kind are prohibited.

Condition of the paths

Restoring the paths of the antica Via del Cifalco to their former splendour required significant work, but maintenance never ends.

We do our best to ensure it on an ongoing basis, through a network of volunteers; however, in some seasons it is truly burdensome. On one stretch in particular, the problems are structural and impossible to eliminate, namely the part of the descent from M. Caucaso to Neirone between the bend at the dry-stone walls and Pian del Pero. This stretch, being dominated by dense vegetation of ferns and heather that thrive wildly with the April and May rains, is often difficult to get through at this time of year. Use of the GPX track is recommended here.

Before setting off, check the websites of the municipalities concerned if you suspect that some stretches of path may be subject to total or partial closure orders.

Mushroom picking

The ridge between the Trebbia and the Aveto up to the summit of M. Caucaso is a paradise for mushroom hunters: you will not be the first to discover it. Strict compliance with the rules laid down by regional legislation is, however, recommended, bearing in mind that it is your responsibility, in border areas, to know whether you are in Emilia or in Liguria. Consider also that the consortia managing the Comunelli set special rules for the consortium lands. They will not fail to punish any violation severely.

Use of guides and other companions

L’Antica Via del Cifalco is open and completely free. Anyone can go there without permits or authorisations.

It is nevertheless possible to walk it, in whole or in part, with a guide. The choice of being accompanied by a guide is purely voluntary and subject only to the guide’s own rates (the promoters have no agreement with any guide).

If you do not have a guide of your own, we would point out that the Guida Ambientale Escursionistica (GAE, environmental hiking guide) Francesca Ciccolini operates in the area; she knows the walk, contributed to its creation and can therefore accompany you along many stretches: francescaciccolini1@gmail.com

Any other guide active in the area who would like their details included on this website is invited to contact us.

Safety and equipment

The use of suitable equipment is recommended, taking into account the chosen season. L’Antica Via del Cifalco is a walk potentially open to everyone, but it is no picnic. We strongly advise against undertaking it if you are out of training or lack the experience needed to complete a hike of several days.

There are no specific dangers on the Way, but please note that in recent years there has been – here as in every other part of the Ligurian Apennines – a marked increase in ticks, which in turn are a consequence of the growth of ungulates (wild boar, roe deer, fallow deer and red deer) in our woods. It is not excessive zeal to inspect your body carefully every evening after walking, especially if for some reason you have left the path and passed through tall grass, got wet in the streams or lain on the ground, even for just a few minutes. If you find a tick, remove it safely straight away and disinfect; monitor the bite for at least two weeks and seek medical assistance without delay should the wound worsen, in particular if the characteristic circular “erythema migrans” appears.

Insect repellents significantly reduce the chances of being bitten, without ever ruling it out altogether.

These same repellents will be good travelling companions in any case, especially in the area between Cerignale and M. delle Tane between the end of August and September, where the presence of flies and gnats at that time of year can be a nuisance.

Respect for nature and fire risk

Be responsible in the woods: avoid any carelessness that could cause harm to people, property, flora and fauna.

In particular, a very delicate matter concerns fires, a true scourge of our times, to which our Apennines are unfortunately no stranger. If you spot a fire, call 112 immediately – Comando Unità Forestali, Ambientali e Agroalimentari (CUFA) of the Arma dei Carabinieri. And if you also find the arsonist and feel like giving him a good thrashing, rest assured that we will not have seen a thing.

Phone signal

Along the whole route there is generally reception and a good 5G signal, although to varying degrees depending on the phone operator. That said, outside emergencies or the need to consult maps, we advise you to look around you rather than stay glued to your smartphones.
